title: Persist restored CMS workflows through an injectable backend
description: Verify the actual restored CMS component paths. Add typed injectable persistence boundaries with an isolated local fixture backend, optimistic concurrency and failure handling. Keep live Amplify/auth and production data disconnected. Inventory every module integration and report exact remaining cloud requirements.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Tested increment f2ca29ef74585815c74deac003485845973e8139: actual shared publication-policy/section editors persist through isolated SQLite with transactional revision/event; failure and concurrent stale-write UI proofs pass. Typed production factory accepts actual generated Amplify client without casts, retains userPool authorization and validates required Item versions/section status. Article/editor/media injection seams added. 12 Python checks; content-action/article/media/backend TypeScript tests; isolated tsc/ESLint/build; CMS ready-render checks, mobile shell, real Kanbus create/move/note/reload, real synthetic Cyclotron labels/accept, typed records/forum regression all pass. Per-module missing integration in docs/unified-cms-integration.md. Full backend carry-forward remains open: category doctrine, reorder, articles/media, taxonomy/ontology, original forums, procedures and actual semantic services. No live privileged CMS data/credentials connected.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Next verified increment be203f245dafa55b584280920b0f63c3158c2b1c: scoped category-policy creation/update uses actual doctrine helper identities and persists/reloads. Section create is durable; failed creation retains draft inputs. Injected section ordering now requires explicit atomic capability; isolated exact-permutation update and event commit together, survives reload, rejects malformed/duplicate/incomplete ids. Shared-component browser structure proof and existing policy failure/conflict/merge proof pass. 14 Python checks, generated-client TypeScript compatibility, adapter contracts, lint/build pass. Public-cloud factory deliberately has no fake atomic reorder capability; production needs an actual atomic host operation. Remaining inventory updated. No live credentials/data, deployment or push.
